chapter: Looking back, big bands and sidemen
title: Would he do it all again? The music is worth it
summary: Herman says he would do it all over, because of the music, stimulation, people and travel.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: We were talking about whether this whole long safari of yours in jazz, big bands, the whole music industry, has been worth it to you.

Well, I've never really tried to make an evaluation, but I do honestly believe that if I had to do it all over again, I would. And I'd probably do it pretty much the same way, and plod through it somehow, as I have.
Uh-huh. What have been the key attributes that make you feel that way, that it's worth doing it all over again?

Well, I think it's the music itself. I think that's the most valuable and most important factor. There's a lot of things you have to give away, such as comfort and relaxation, and to a great extent -- but there are things that I think more than make up for it, too, in the fact that you receive a great amount of stimulation from the music and from people, from audiences, and from the travel to every corner of the earth.
So you have to pay some dues for whatever you get.
